newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia vows to be leading regional finance hub.
newsitem.headline: Australia vows to be leading regional finance hub.

text.p: Australia vowed on Friday to oertake Hong Kong and Singapore as a leading Asia-Pacific financial centre next century.

"We are committed to making Australia the second financial centre of the region after Tokyo for the 21st century," Prime Minister John Howard said, setting the scene for a more interventionist industry policy.
Howard accepted three industries recommended for government assistance in a recent inquiry -- telecommunications, resource processing and tourism.
"I would add information technology/online services and the financial services industry," Howard told an industry dinner.
"Some of these sectors will be the subject of decisions over the next few months which will accelerate their development."
Industry policy has come back into fashion a little in Australia, having been derided for years as akin to the government trying to bet on favourite industries as if they were horses in a race.
But Howard said: "This is not picking winners -- it is facilitating the emergence of new areas of competitive advantage."
Opinion pollsters have recently detected rapidly growing public enthusiasm for industry policy.
This mounting support has been driven particularly by the announced closure of a steelworks earlier this year and an evident weariness among Australians for microeconomic reform.
The government is already partly through a set of policy initiatives intended to streamline the financial sector.

"(These) reforms could yield cost savings for the economy of up to A$4 billion (US$3 billion) a year, provide more competitive financial services and allow the industry to achieve its potential as a regional financial centre," Howard said.
Australia currently trails Tokyo, Hong Kong and Singapore.
But the pollsters have found that Australians are mostly interested in industries that make things.

Many were disturbed when earlier this year the Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said it would close one its three steelworks, at the provincial city of Newcastle, north of Sydney, which had been one of Australia's early attempts at downstream mineral processing.

At the time, the government said this was ultimately a business decision, but on Friday Howard included exactly that sector of the economy -- resource processing -- as a target for government assistance.
But Howard did not describe precisely how he planned to support the five industry sectors he listed.
The conservative Liberal-National government is due soon to detail its response to the industry policy report.
